title: model-loading-shard-download-issue-notes
content:
Summary:
Observed repeated model load failures in staging when loading redwood/llama-13b-v2 (sharded weights). Symptoms point to incomplete/failed weights shard downloads from our S3/CloudFront pipeline (403/503 and EOF errors). This doc is my scratchpad for repro steps, logs, commands tried, hypotheses, and next actions.

Timeline (local timestamps PST):
- 2026-02-15 09:12 — First alert: canary load failed with 500 from serving-runtime (model load).
- 2026-02-15 09:14 — Tried manual restart of runtime; same failure.
- 2026-02-15 09:17 — Started manual debug from a staging box (ec2-staging-12).

Commands I ran (repro):
1) curl of presigned URL for shard_07.safetensors:
   curl -v -o shard_07.safetensors "https://cdn.redwood-inference.com/models/redwood/llama-13b-v2/shard_07.safetensors?X-Amz-..."
   -> result: HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden (presigned URL expired).

2) aws s3 cp to the internal S3 mirror (same object):
   aws s3 cp s3://models-prod/redwood/llama-13b-v2/shard_07.safetensors ./shard_07.safetensors
   -> result: Completed sometimes; on repeated runs: sometimes returns 200 but file size is smaller than expected (partial).

3) verified sizes and checksums:
   - expected size (from index.json): 2147483648 bytes
   - downloaded size (partial): 1288490188 bytes (approx 1.2GB)
   - sha256 checks: expected sha256 in index.json vs computed -> mismatch (partial file).

Observed errors in runtime logs when attempting to load the partial shard (serving-runtime stderr):
- safetensors.errors.SafetensorError: Unexpected EOF while reading tensor data (file truncated)
- traceback shows file read failing inside safetensors.load_file -> file mapping -> read buffer

Other failures seen across different nodes:
- boto3.exceptions.S3UploadFailedError / ClientError: 503 Service Unavailable (CloudFront origin returning 503 intermittently)
- urllib3.exceptions.ProtocolError: ('Connection aborted.', RemoteDisconnected('Remote end closed connection without response'))

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Presigned URL TTL/regeneration bug: index.json contains presigned URLs generated at model push time; some TTLs are too short or the generator is using a server clock that skews expiration. (Likely — saw 403s).
2) Upstream storage (S3 -> CloudFront) transient errors causing partial downloads (503s, truncated reads).
3) Client-side downloader (our runtime's async fetcher) isn't retrying / resuming properly and is accepting partial files as 'complete' if write streams close early.
4) Checkpoint packaging bug: one of the shards uploaded incorrectly (truncated at upload). Less likely — upload logs show success but need to confirm ETag/content-length.
5) Naming mismatch from recent PR (#456) caused index.json -> shard file mapping mismatch, leading to requests pointing to the wrong (deleted) object.

Evidence & quick checks:
- index.json snippet: contains presigned URLs with expiry param X-Amz-Expires=3600, generated at 2026-02-15T08:10:00Z. Canary load at 09:12 failed -> >60m, explains 403s. So presigned TTL set to 1 hour but model push -> canary run exceeded that window.
- S3 head-object on shard_07 shows Content-Length=2147483648 and ETag="abc123" in primary bucket (confirm upload present). The mirror bucket (s3://models-prod) sometimes shows smaller Content-Length on certain replicas temporarily.
- CloudFront logs show 503 origin errors for a handful of requests at 2026-02-15 09:10-09:20.

Commands / outputs (raw snippets):
$ curl -I "<presigned-url-expired>"
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 09:13:02 GMT
Server: AmazonS3

$ aws s3api head-object --bucket models-prod --key redwood/llama-13b-v2/shard_07.safetensors
{
  "ContentLength": 2147483648,
  "ETag": "\"abc123\"",
  "LastModified": "2026-02-15T07:59:02+00:00"
}

$ sha256sum shard_07.safetensors.partial
<computed-sha>  shard_07.safetensors.partial
(does not match expected in index.json)

What I tried to fix (and results):
- Regenerated presigned URLs for the model (storage infra): new URLs fixed 403s. After using new URLs, downloads completed with correct sizes. Temporary fix worked for canary.
- Added retries to the fetcher (simple retry x3) — reduced frequency of partial files but didn't cure presigned expiry problem.
- Forcing a reupload of shard_07 from source artifact store (artifact-store -> s3 copy) — confirmed object matches expected checksum.
- Verified that the runtime commit at HEAD includes the recent downloader changes from PR #445; PR #456 changed index generation naming and might have created a race where presigned URLs are generated too early during model push.

Potential root causes (combined):
- Presigned URL TTL too short for our model push -> indexing -> propagation -> canary timeline (we generate presigned URLs at push time rather than request time).
- CloudFront intermittent origin 503s leading to partial downloads if client isn't robust to truncated streams.
- Our fetcher was marking downloads as complete when file descriptor closed; no final checksum/size verification before handing off to loader.

Immediate mitigations (applied):
- Regenerated presigned URLs on staging models.
- Added quick checksum verification step in the local fetcher path (size + sha256) and abort load on mismatch (will patch runtime in staging branch).
- Increased presigned URL TTL to 6 hours for model pushes while we fix generation timing.

Longer-term fixes / TODOs:
- (ENG-STORAGE) Change presigned URL generation to happen lazily (on-demand) at load time or ensure TTL covers worst-case push->deploy timeline. Ticket: JIRA-INC-2026-84 (assigned to Aisha).
- (ENG-SERVING) Harden downloader: support resuming ranged GETs, verify content-length/sha256 before moving to final path; atomic rename only on verified files. (PR target: serving-runtime#467).
- (ENG-RELEASE) Add a post-push validation step that HEADs all shard objects and verifies content-length/etag match index.json before marking model as "published".
- Add automated alerting when shard download returns 4xx/5xx > threshold during canary window.

Notes for postmortem:
- Likely low-severity but could impact customers during model rollout windows. Need to update runbook for model push and scale checks for TTL.
- Consider instrumenting per-shard download metrics (success rate, bytes transferred, retries) in console.

Next actions (me):
- [ ] Draft PR for checksum verification + atomic rename (start branch: mw/shard-checksum).
- [ ] Coordinate with storage infra to change URL generation strategy (sync w/ Aisha).
- [ ] Add regression test that simulates expired presigned URL and verifies loader handles it gracefully.
- [ ] Add one-off job to revalidate published models for the last 7 days (catch other bad pushes).

Open questions / unknowns:
- Did any model pushes in last 48 hours generate presigned URLs with TTL=1h? Which CI job sets TTL? (Search: model-push pipeline, artifact-uploader).
- Is there an upstream S3 replication delay that causes the mirror to have partial content for a short window? (Investigate replication metrics).

If anyone wants to pick this up: see linked JIRA + PRs. Ping me in #serving-runtime or Slack thread referenced above.

End of notes.
